citation: Harsha, Phogat, Dasaratha, Puranam & Ramakrishna (2025), FinNLP-FNP-LLMFinLegal workshop, pp. 76-95. Read: ACL Anthology page and full PDF text incl. appendices
text_source: Same report pages as FinQA (S&P 500 annual reports 1999-2019), TATQA hybrid contexts, ConvFinQA; synthetic sets sized to train splits (6,251 / 4,992 / 2,737)
feature: GPT-4o writes questions from each page (temp 0.7, earlier questions in prompt) and Python answers (temp 0); filter on executable scalar output only; numeric QA, auto-graded by execution
method: LoRA SFT of Phi-3-mini 3.8B, Phi-3-medium 14B, Mistral-7B on synthetic vs real data; data-size ladder 750-full; nearest vs farthest synthetic questions; real/synthetic mixes
outcome: FinQA test: Phi-3-mini 68.43 synthetic vs 73.49 real; Phi-3-medium 73.49 vs 77.59; Mistral 67.21 vs 76.63. TATQA within 1-3 points. Cross-set: synthetic FinQA -> TATQA 84.26 vs real 81.19. Phi-3-mini synthetic 750/1.5K/3K/full 63.99/64.95/68.61/68.43. <5% of audited synthetic questions Boolean or text-only; students weakest there. ConvFinQA 10% real + 90% synthetic 69.98 vs all real 76.00
incremental_to: Same students trained on expert-written data of equal size
pit_handling: Not addressed; whether test-split pages fed generation not stated
informs_decision: Teacher-written questions from the filings can replace expert data for 3.8B+ students on numeric QA and transfer better across data sets; generator's question-type bias reappears as student weakness (S1's label-item lock-in); gains flatten after ~3K items of one family

citation: Yang, Band, Li, Candes & Hashimoto (2025), ICLR 2025; arXiv 2409.07431v2 (EntiGraph, synthetic continued pretraining). Read: abstract, v2 HTML incl. appendices C-H, ICLR poster page
text_source: QuALITY: 265 articles/books, 1.3M tokens; 455M synthetic tokens by gpt-4-turbo
feature: Entity extraction then text on relations among sampled entity pairs and triples, grounded in each document; closed-book four-option QA (auto-graded), summaries (claim-level judge)
method: Continued pretraining of Llama 3 8B (2 epochs, 10% RedPajama replay) on EntiGraph text vs raw text vs rephrasing vs synthetic QA; then instruction tuning; RAG combination
outcome: Closed-book 39.49 (base) -> 56.22 (EntiGraph 455M tokens) vs GPT-4 51.30; raw CPT below base; rephrase scales poorly; log-linear in synthetic tokens, no plateau reached; with RAG 62.60 vs 60.35
pit_handling: Not relevant (fiction/journalism); method memorises the corpus by design
informs_decision: Document-grounded synthesis teaches a model what a corpus says where raw text does not, with returns rising in volume; diversity from prompt structure (entity pairs). Knowledge, not reasoning; generator faithfulness credited to gpt-4-turbo

citation: Cheng, Gu, Huang, Bi, Huang & Wei (2024), EMNLP 2024; arXiv 2406.14491v2 (Instruction Pre-Training). Read: abstract and v2 HTML (about 92%)
text_source: RefinedWeb 100B tokens (from scratch); PubMed abstracts and financial news (domain); 200M synthesized pairs over 40+ task categories
feature: Mistral-7B 'instruction synthesizer' tuned on ~34 reading data sets writes ~5 instruction-response pairs (~52 tokens) per raw text, multi-round; finance eval ConvFinQA, FPB, FiQA SA, Headline, NER
method: Pre-training 500M/1.3B from scratch and continued pre-training of Llama3-8B on raw text + synthesized pairs vs raw text; ablations vs rule-mined tasks and one-shot synthesis
outcome: Finance avg: Llama3-8B 70.1, raw CPT 72.0, Instruct PT 74.7, Llama3-70B 71.9; rule-mined 73.1; 500M 45.1->46.6, 1.3B 48.6->49.7 (9-benchmark avg); finance pairs correct 69.8% (GPT-4 judge), 73.5% (human)
incremental_to: Raw-text continued pre-training; rule-based task mining (AdaptLLM); Llama3-70B
pit_handling: Not addressed; finance corpus undated in text read and not public
informs_decision: A 7B generator writing many short varied tasks per domain document beats raw-text training in finance, and model-written tasks beat rule-mined ones; gain survives ~30% wrong pairs. Closest published design to 'teacher writes many Q&A per 8-K release'

citation: Liu, Bubeck, Eldan, Kulkarni, Li, Nguyen, Ward & Zhang (2023), arXiv 2312.09241v1 (TinyGSM), preprint. Read: abstract and v1 HTML
text_source: Comparable domain (math): 12.3M GPT-3.5-turbo problems with Python solutions (~1.8B tokens, ~$3,600) seeded from 7,473 GSM8K train questions; 13-gram contamination check
feature: Grade-school math word problems; answers by code execution; correctness of generated answers not checked
method: Full fine-tuning of Phi-1.5-family 125M/350M/1.3B; separate verifier (same sizes) trained on 48 generations per GSM8K train question; best of 48 at test
outcome: Generator alone: 125M 63.1, 350M 65.9, 1.3B 68.2; 1.3B+1.3B verifier 81.5 vs GPT-3.5 teacher 77.4; 125M gen + 1.3B verifier 76.1 > 1.3B gen + 125M verifier 71.7; 1/3 -> 2/3 of data '10% increase' (points or relative not stated), last third marginal; SVAMP 75.6
incremental_to: Random-init students; larger open models; teacher
pit_handling: n-gram decontamination (22 of 11.0M at 13-gram); paraphrase contamination unsolved
informs_decision: Massive teacher-generated data makes a sub-1B model strong on one narrow verifiable task family; flattens between ~8M and 12M items; verifier scaling beats generator scaling. Says nothing about breadth across answer types

citation: Guha, Marten, Keh, Raoof, Smyrnis, Bansal and 44 others (2025), arXiv 2506.04178v2 (OpenThoughts), preprint. Read: abstract and v2 HTML (about 86%)
text_source: Comparable domains (math, code, science): OpenThoughts3-1.2M (850K/250K/100K), traces ~11.6K tokens; decontaminated benchmarks
feature: Supervised reasoning-trace data recipe: question source, mixing, filtering, answers per question, answer filtering, teacher
method: 1,000+ controlled SFT runs at 31.6K examples on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, then scale to 1.2M; Llama-3.1-8B as second base
outcome: Teacher QwQ-32B > DeepSeek-R1 (code 44.2 vs 42.3; math 44.2 vs 41.6; science 53.2 vs 46.7); 16 answers/question >= more questions; top-2 code sources 41.3 vs top-16 36.4; answer verification no gain (41.9 all vs 40.0 GPT-verified); scaling continues to 1.2M; truncating traces >2,048 tokens -33.3% at 7B
incremental_to: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B and other open data sets
pit_handling: Two-check decontamination of benchmarks (99.6% true-negative rate)
informs_decision: Teacher choice must be tested (stronger model not better teacher); many answers per question is a cheap volume lever; source quality over count; long traces help at 7B (contrast li-2025 below 3B)

citation: Hsieh, Li, Yeh, Nakhost, Fujii, Ratner, Krishna, Lee & Pfister (2023), Findings of ACL 2023; arXiv 2305.02301v2 (Distilling step-by-step). Read: abstract page and Anthology PDF text (parts)
text_source: e-SNLI, ANLI, CommonsenseQA, SVAMP; PaLM 540B rationales
feature: Teacher rationales used as a second training target (multi-task: predict label, generate rationale); label-only output at inference
method: T5 220M/770M/11B; vs standard fine-tuning and label-only distillation; data ladders
outcome: 220M beats standard fine-tuning on 100% of e-SNLI with 12.5% of data; 770M beats few-shot PaLM 540B on ANLI with 80% of data, standard fine-tuning fails with 100%; >50% fewer examples on average
incremental_to: Standard fine-tuning; label distillation; few-shot PaLM
informs_decision: Rationales as an auxiliary target cut data needs for sub-1B students; answer format at test can stay short. Classification and small math only

citation: Ho, Schmid & Yun (2023), ACL 2023; arXiv 2212.10071v2 (Large Language Models Are Reasoning Teachers). Read: abstract page and Anthology PDF text (Table 1, Section on diverse reasoning)
text_source: 12 reasoning tasks (arithmetic, symbolic, date, commonsense); teacher text-davinci-002 zero-shot CoT
feature: Fine-tune-CoT: student trained on teacher CoT; 'diverse reasoning' = 1-64 sampled rationales per question
method: GPT-3 0.3B/1.3B/6.7B and other students; vs vanilla fine-tuning and prompting
outcome: 0.3B student MultiArith 6.11 -> 23.89 and SVAMP 5.00 -> 14.33 with diverse reasoning; teacher MultiArith 78.89; students beat the 175B teacher on Shuffled Objects and Coin Flip
informs_decision: Several teacher rationales per question is a strong, cheap lever even at 0.3B

citation: Mitra, Del Corro, Mahajan and 12 others (2023), arXiv 2311.11045v2 (Orca 2), preprint. Read: abstract and v2 HTML (first half)
text_source: ~817K synthetic instances on FLAN-v2 tasks plus Orca 1 data (5M ChatGPT, 1M GPT-4)
feature: Explanation tuning with task-specific strategies (step-by-step, recall-then-generate, direct answer); 'prompt erasure' hides the strategy prompt from the student
method: LLaMA-2 7B and 13B students; 15 benchmarks, ~100 tasks, 36K prompts, zero-shot
outcome: Orca-2-13B AGIEval 49.93, BBH 50.18 vs LLaMA-2-Chat-70B 46.70, 44.68; Orca-2-7B matches or beats LLaMA-2-Chat-70B on reasoning tasks (authors)
informs_decision: Teaching the student to choose among several answer strategies, rather than one template, is an explicit design against template lock-in; students 7B+

citation: Gunasekar, Zhang, Aneja and 16 others (2023), arXiv 2306.11644v2 (Textbooks Are All You Need; phi-1), preprint. Read: abstract page
text_source: ~6B tokens filtered 'textbook quality' web code + ~1B tokens GPT-3.5 synthetic textbooks and exercises
feature: Pre-training a code model mostly on curated and synthetic text
method: phi-1 1.3B (4 days, 8 A100) and phi-1-small 350M; fine-tuning on synthetic exercises
outcome: phi-1 HumanEval 50.6%, MBPP 55.5%; phi-1-small 350M HumanEval 45%
informs_decision: Synthetic, didactic data can make 0.35-1.3B models strong in one domain; requires pre-training scale, not feasible for S1

citation: Ye, Huang, Xiao, Chern, Xia & Liu (2025), COLM 2025; arXiv 2502.03387v3 (LIMO). Read: abstract and v3 HTML
text_source: Comparable domain (math): 800 curated problems from a 2,125 pool filtered from tens of millions; traces <16K tokens
feature: Small, carefully selected reasoning set; 'LIMO hypothesis' (reasoning elicited if pre-trained knowledge is present)
method: Full SFT of Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct; size ladder 3B-72B; Qwen1.5-32B vs Qwen2.5-32B; 400-2,000 examples
outcome: 32B: AIME24 63.3, MATH500 95.6; same data on Qwen2.5-3B AIME24 2.5; Qwen1.5-32B 9.2 vs Qwen2.5-32B 63.3; 400/800/2,000 examples AIME24 57.5/63.3/69.6
incremental_to: Models trained on ~100x more data; backbones
informs_decision: Small curated sets work only when the base already knows the domain; at 3B the same data gives almost nothing. Rules out 'a few hundred perfect examples' for a 0.8B

citation: Muennighoff, Yang, Shi, Li, Fei-Fei, Hajishirzi, Zettlemoyer, Liang, Candes & Hashimoto (2025), arXiv 2501.19393v3 (s1), preprint. Read: abstract and v3 HTML (about 70%)
text_source: Comparable domain: s1K, 1,000 of 59,029 questions (16 sources), traces by Gemini 2.0 Flash Thinking
feature: Selection by quality, difficulty, diversity; budget forcing at inference
method: SFT of Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct (26 min on 16 H100); ablations random/diverse/longest 1K and full 59K
outcome: AIME24: s1K 50.0, 59K-full 53.3 (394 vs ~7 H100-hours), 1K-random 36.7, 1K-diverse 26.7, 1K-longest 33.3; no student below 32B
incremental_to: Random, diverse-only, longest-only subsets; full pool
informs_decision: At 32B, selection gets most of the full-pool gain at ~2% of the compute; diversity alone was the worst selector. No evidence for sub-3B students

citation: Busbridge, Shidani, Weers, Ramapuram, Littwin & Webb (2025), ICML 2025; arXiv 2502.08606v2 (Distillation Scaling Laws). Read: abstract and v2 HTML (first 30%)
text_source: Pre-training-scale distillation; students and teachers 143M-12.6B, a few billion to 512B tokens
feature: Logit distillation in pre-training; student loss as a function of teacher loss and compute split
method: Fitted scaling law over IsoFLOP and fixed-teacher sweeps
outcome: Capacity gap: past a point a stronger teacher gives a worse student (U-shape in teacher size, driven by teacher cross-entropy); distillation beats supervised learning only below a compute level that grows with student size, or when a teacher already exists
informs_decision: Teacher too far above student hurts; with existing teachers (S1's case) distillation is the efficient choice at small compute

citation: Cheng, Huang & Wei (2024), ICLR 2024; arXiv 2309.09530v4 (AdaptLLM, reading comprehension). Read: abstract and v4 HTML
text_source: Financial news May 2022-May 2023, >7,000 stocks, ~1.2B tokens (FinGPT codebase); also biomedicine and law
feature: Raw domain text converted by regex rules into reading-comprehension tasks (summarise, word-to-text, NLI, commonsense, paraphrase, completion); mixed with general instructions (ratio garbled in the text read)
method: Continued pre-training of LLaMA-7B; vs raw-text continued pre-training
outcome: Finance avg (ConvFinQA, FPB, FiQA SA, Headline, NER): LLaMA-7B 58.6, raw-text DAPT 57.6, AdaptLLM 63.4, BloombergGPT-50B 62.5; ConvFinQA 29.2 -> 41.5
informs_decision: Raw domain text alone lowers prompted ability; turning each text into tasks about it restores and raises it, even with rule-based tasks

citation: Allen-Zhu & Li (2024), arXiv 2309.14316v3 (Physics of Language Models Part 3.1: Knowledge Storage and Extraction), preprint. Read: abstract page
text_source: Controlled synthetic biography corpus
feature: Whether knowledge seen in pre-training can be extracted by questions; effect of augmentation (paraphrase, shuffling, translation)
method: Training from scratch with and without augmentation; probing
outcome: Without augmentation knowledge is memorised but extraction accuracy is 0% regardless of later instruction tuning; extraction tracks training-data diversity
informs_decision: Mechanism behind EntiGraph and Instruction Pre-Training: one phrasing per fact is not learnable as usable knowledge; restatements in varied form are

citation: Zhang, Wang & Charton (2024), arXiv 2402.10891v1 (Instruction Diversity Drives Generalization To Unseen Tasks), preprint. Read: abstract and v1 HTML
text_source: Synthetic string-rewriting tasks (Markov-algorithm rules); encrypted rewriting with Llama-2-7b
feature: Number of distinct instructions vs examples per instruction, at fixed budget (~10^6 examples); semantic classes of rules
method: Small GPT-2 from scratch; Llama-2-7b LoRA
outcome: No generalisation to unseen instructions below ~300 instructions at ~10^6 examples; transition ~400-500; always generalises at >=1,000 even with few examples each; models trained on few instructions default to the no-op answer; one semantic class of rules does not generalise, a mix does; long-tailed instruction mixes hurt at 1,000 instructions, little at 10^4-10^5
incremental_to: Fewer instructions with more examples each
informs_decision: Diversity of task types, not volume per type, buys transfer to unseen tasks; low diversity makes the model fall back on a default output (cf. S1's boxed number on 300/300 label items)

citation: Fu, Peng, Ou, Sabharwal & Khot (2023), ICML 2023, PMLR 202:10421-10430; arXiv 2301.12726v1 (Specializing Smaller Language Models towards Multi-Step Reasoning). Read: PMLR page and arXiv PDF text (Sections 1-4)
text_source: Comparable domain (math): GSM8K 7K questions x 40 code-davinci-002 solutions, correct kept = 130K
feature: Specialising a small model on one skill; four data formats (in-context or zero-shot, answer-only or CoT); generic ability on BigBench Hard
method: FlanT5 and T5 250M-11B fine-tuned on teacher CoT; checkpoint selection in vs out of distribution
outcome: FlanT5 gains ~+10 on math (11B GSM8K 16.1 -> 27.1; 4-set avg 40.8 vs LaMDA-137B 35.9); BBH CoT drops to 0 at the first checkpoint; zero-shot-format data removes in-context ability, in-context data keeps both; FlanT5-3B plateaus ~90K examples, smaller models need more epochs; in-dist vs OOD checkpoint choice trades ~2 points
informs_decision: A small model can beat much larger ones on one skill by giving up generic ability; the format of training data decides which abilities survive. Matches S1's FinQA drop and single-format lock-in

citation: Xu, Jiang, Niu, Lin & Poovendran (2025), NAACL 2025; arXiv 2411.07133v3 (Stronger Models are NOT Stronger Teachers for Instruction Tuning). Read: abstract and v3 HTML
text_source: Synthetic instruction sets (e.g. Mix-100K) answered by 20 generators from 7 families (Qwen2/2.5, Llama 3/3.1, Gemma 2, Phi-3, GPT-4)
feature: Which teacher's responses make the best instruction-tuning data for 1.5B-4B students
method: SFT of Qwen2-1.5B, Gemma-2-2b, Llama-3.2-3B, Qwen2.5-3B, Llama-3.1-Minitron-4B; AlpacaEval 2 and Arena-Hard; CAR metric
outcome: Minitron-4B: Gemma-2-9b-it 14.90 vs Gemma-2-27b-it 13.17; GPT-4 5.72 (all open teachers higher); same-family teachers best for Qwen2-1.5B, Qwen2.5-3B, Gemma-2-2B; not uniform (Qwen2.5-72B 16.15 > 7B 12.05); CAR Spearman 0.889 avg
informs_decision: For sub-4B students a larger teacher is not reliably better; same-family teachers help; compatibility with the student predicts usefulness

citation: Zhang, Li, Song, Ye, Gao & Hu (2025), ACL 2025; arXiv 2311.07052v4 (Towards the Law of Capacity Gap in Distilling Language Models). Read: abstract and v4 HTML (about 75%)
text_source: OpenWebText ~3.9B tokens (pilot); 126B tokens (MiniMA)
feature: Optimal teacher size for a given student under pruning + logit distillation
method: Pilot with GPT-2 and Pythia teachers 70M-2.8B; MiniMA 3B from LLaMA2-7B
outcome: Optimal teacher T* ~ 2.5 x student (fit 2.498 S - 11.498, R2 0.996); MiniMA degrades when the teacher grows from LLaMA2-7B to 13B and 70B
informs_decision: For a 0.8B student the optimum under this law is ~2B; 4B is ~5x. Fit on pre-training-style logit KD, not reasoning SFT

citation: Chen, Sun, Guo, Zhang, Chen, Sun, Su, Pan, Klakow, Li & Shen (2025), Findings of ACL 2025; arXiv 2502.18001v3 (Unveiling the Key Factors for Distilling Chain-of-Thought Reasoning). Read: abstract and v3 HTML (about 88%)
text_source: Math (SVAMP, GSM8K, AQuA, MATH) and commonsense (CSQA, OpenBookQA, StrategyQA); teachers GPT-4o, Gemini-1.5-Flash, LLaMA-3-70B, humans
feature: CoT granularity (levels), CoT format, teacher choice for small students
method: SFT of BLOOM 560M/1.1B/1.7B/3B, Gemma 2B, LLaMA-3.2 1B/3B
outcome: Weak students peak at intermediate granularity, stronger ones at fine (Gemma-2B SVAMP 59.00 -> 67.11); padding length does not reproduce granularity gains (GSM8K 46.62 vs 52.92); format matters little; teacher-student accuracy correlation r 0.25-0.64; LLM CoT beats more accurate human CoT on math
informs_decision: For students near 1B, keep traces simple and pick the teacher empirically; teacher accuracy is a weak guide

citation: Yang, Li, Yang and 57 others (2025), arXiv 2505.09388v1 (Qwen3 Technical Report). Read: abstract and v1 HTML (strong-to-weak distillation section, Table 21)
text_source: Qwen3 post-training data (not public)
feature: Strong-to-weak distillation for 0.6B-14B dense and 30B-A3B: off-policy (teacher responses in think/no-think modes) then on-policy (student samples, logits aligned to teacher by KL)
method: Teachers Qwen3-32B or 235B-A22B; Table 21 compares RL vs on-policy distillation on Qwen3-8B
outcome: Qwen3-8B after off-policy distillation AIME24 55.0; + RL 67.6 (17,920 GPU-h); + on-policy distillation 74.4 (1,800 GPU-h); pass@64 rises only with distillation (90.0 -> 93.3)
informs_decision: The model family S1 uses was itself built by off-policy then on-policy logit distillation from a larger sibling; on-policy distillation beat RL at 1/10 of the compute

citation: DeepSeek-AI (Guo et al.) (2025), Nature 645:633-638; arXiv 2501.12948 (DeepSeek-R1). Read: abstract page (v2) and v1 HTML distillation section (Tables 5-6)
text_source: 800K samples curated with DeepSeek-R1
feature: SFT-only distillation of long reasoning traces into dense models
method: Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B/7B, Qwen2.5-14B/32B, Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3.3-70B; no RL on students; RL-only Qwen-32B for comparison
outcome: R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B AIME24 28.9, MATH-500 83.9, GPQA-D 33.8; 7B 55.5 / 92.8 / 49.1; Qwen-32B distilled 72.6 vs RL-only 47.0 on AIME24
incremental_to: Large-scale RL on the same base
informs_decision: Large-volume distillation beats RL for small dense models in math; the 1.5B started from a math-specialised base. 13a records the same models lose to their instruct bases on finance (liu-2025)

citation: Agarwal, Vieillard, Zhou, Stanczyk, Ramos, Geist & Bachem (2024), ICLR 2024; arXiv 2306.13649v3 (GKD: On-Policy Distillation of Language Models). Read: abstract and v3 HTML
text_source: XSum, WMT14 en-de, GSM8K (CoT); FLAN for task-agnostic instruction tuning
feature: On-policy distillation: student samples its own outputs, teacher scores them token by token; choice of divergence
method: Teacher T5-XL (~3B); students T5-small 77M, base 250M, large 800M; vs supervised KD, sequence-level KD
outcome: On-policy gain over initial student is 2.1x (summarisation), 1.7x (translation), 1.9x (GSM8K) the gain of baseline KD; on GSM8K better as student-generated share rises (>=25%); reverse KL best for instruction tuning (+2 BBH, +1 MMLU held-out)
informs_decision: For sub-1B students, training on the student's own samples scored by the teacher beats imitating fixed teacher text; needs teacher logits (same tokenizer)

citation: Ke, Ming, Nguyen, Xiong & Joty (2025), EMNLP 2025; arXiv 2501.04961v4 (FinDAP / Llama-Fin). Read: abstract and v4 HTML (about 75%)
text_source: ~6B tokens financial text (70 websites and books) plus general data; ~3M IT prompts, GPT-4o responses where missing; ~32K CFA-prep prompts for preference data
feature: Domain-adaptive post-training: joint continued pre-training + instruction tuning, then DPO with GPT-4o as generative reward model
method: Llama3-8B-Instruct -> Llama-Fin (8B); FinEval with similar and novel tasks
outcome: FPB 91.13 vs 73.09; CFA-Challenge 55.56 vs 34.44; better than base on 13 of 17 novel finance tasks; CPT alone collapses MT-Bench to ~1 vs 7.89, joint CPT+IT keeps 7.36
informs_decision: Finance post-training with teacher-written responses generalises to novel finance tasks at 8B if domain text and instructions are trained jointly; raw domain text alone wrecks instruction following
